title: Finding a customer by company name
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header click the Search box (it is a BUTTON, data-test-id global_search_trigger, not a typeable field) or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K. Global search opens as a CENTRED MODAL over the page: a text input at the top, then a scope tab strip - All, Work orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part sales, Purchase orders, Vendor invoices - each showing its own result count, then results grouped by type with a count beside each heading (e.g. "Work orders (4)"). Esc closes the modal. NOTE: group headings are SENTENCE case in the build ("Work orders", "Part sales"). If a group shows nothing, click that entity's scope tab to confirm it really is 0 rather than scrolling. Modal behaviour verified on the V2 QA branch sv9160 on 14 September 2026.
1. The customer 'ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling' exists.
2. Customers access: View.
custom_steps:
1. Open global search.
2. Type a distinctive word from the company name: Bridgeport
3. Read the Customers group.
4. Clear the input and type the full name: ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling
5. Read the Customers group again.
custom_expected:
Both searches return the customer 'ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling'.
This is the most basic thing global search does and the control for every other customer case on this suite - if this fails, nothing else about customers can be trusted.
IF THIS FAILS: it is a real V1-to-V2 capability loss. Mark the test Blocked with the exact query you typed and what came back, and flag it - a task ticket goes to the Product Owner to confirm whether the loss is acceptable. Do not raise it as a defect until the PO has ruled, and do not pass the test just because the V2 specification allows the new behaviour.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the V1 behaviour recorded in the ShopView code baseline 55767168 (FetchDataQueryHandler.php:224-245, where c.name is the label and is also folded into the customer search text). Version 1.5 of the specification (Confluence page 576978945) section 4 indexes the customer name.

title: Finding an asset by its VIN, in full and in part
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header click the Search box (it is a BUTTON, data-test-id global_search_trigger, not a typeable field) or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K. Global search opens as a CENTRED MODAL over the page: a text input at the top, then a scope tab strip - All, Work orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part sales, Purchase orders, Vendor invoices - each showing its own result count, then results grouped by type with a count beside each heading (e.g. "Work orders (4)"). If a group shows nothing, click that entity's scope tab to confirm it really is 0 rather than scrolling. Modal behaviour verified on the V2 QA branch sv9160 on 14 September 2026.
1. The asset with VIN '1FUJGLDR9KLZZ4471', unit 'ZZT-4471', exists.
2. Customers access: View.
custom_steps:
1. Open global search.
2. Type the COMPLETE VIN: 1FUJGLDR9KLZZ4471
3. Read the Assets group.
4. Clear the input and type the last part of the VIN only: ZZ4471
5. Read the Assets group again.
custom_expected:
Both searches return the asset.
In V1 the VIN was matched anywhere inside the record's search text, so the whole VIN and any piece of it both worked - a technician reading the last six characters off a windscreen plate could find the vehicle.
THIS CASE IS EXPECTED TO FAIL ON THE CURRENT BUILD, AND IN A STRANGE WAY. On 14 September 2026 the complete VIN returned NOTHING while the first eleven characters '1FUJGLDR9KL' DID return the asset. If you see exactly that, mark FAILED and raise nothing new - it is already reported. Fails differently: a NEW problem, report it. Passes: the fix shipped, tell the QA lead.
IF THIS FAILS: it is a real V1-to-V2 capability loss. Mark the test Blocked with the exact query you typed and what came back, and flag it - a task ticket goes to the Product Owner to confirm whether the loss is acceptable. Do not raise it as a defect until the PO has ruled, and do not pass the test just because the V2 specification allows the new behaviour.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the V1 behaviour recorded in the ShopView code baseline 55767168 (FetchDataQueryHandler.php:292 (v.vin folded into the asset search text) with useGlobalSearch.ts:92 (matched anywhere inside it)). Version 1.5 of the specification (Confluence page 576978945) section 4 indexes VIN and section 7 requires an exact match after normalization - so the complete VIN returning nothing is a build defect. Whether a PART of a VIN should still match is the V1 behaviour this suite protects.
Standing Rule 96 makes a V1 capability the default expectation and Standing Rule 58 makes a code-versus-document conflict a PO DECISION ITEM, so this case asserts the V1 behaviour and tells you to record and flag rather than guess.
